properties.description:
Given the upstream exports this design named in its OWN committed manifest, opens each one, computes its content hash from content, and reports what was found — so the comparison living in `cmp:depends` has something to judge. Implemented in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/upstream.rs`.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A FUNCTION AND NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly, so the module holding the judgement CANNOT open a file. This is the half that can. It is the same split `reconcile_dependencies` and `reconcile_artifacts` already make, where the caller supplies what it observed and the core judges it.

⚠️ THREE PROHIBITIONS, EACH ONE LOAD-BEARING:
- IT DOES NOT NAVIGATE. Every path opened is one this design pointed at ITSELF, in its own committed manifest. reflow2 does no file navigation; reading a self-declared path does not breach that rule, and searching for candidates would.
- IT DOES NOT WRITE. Not the baseline, not a sync record. A read that refreshed what it compares against would report `moved` once and then go permanently quiet.
- IT DOES NOT IMPORT. Importing a design into a store that already holds one keeps the HOST's name and upserts the incoming nodes into it, which ABSORBS the child — exactly what the hub case forbids. This looks without taking.

⚠️ ABSENCE IS REPORTED, NEVER ASSUMED. `never_seen`, `missing`, `unreadable`, `graph_id_mismatch` and `not_observed` are distinct answers, so a pass that found nothing can never be read as a pass that found nothing WRONG. The pass is bounded at 16 exports and NAMES what it skipped.

📌 IT SATISFIES THE SAME REQUIREMENT AS `cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `req:design-dependencies-declared` names two checks; "has what I depend on moved since" is unanswerable without this reading. Two capabilities against one requirement is the honest shape here — the requirement asks for a check, and the check has a judging half and a looking half. No new need was invented to justify this part.
properties.name: What a declared upstream actually holds is read where it lies — without navigating to it, writing to it, or taking it in
